category_title: Student with language impairment who uses loud noises and physical aggression to avoid tasks
minimal_context: Terrance is assigned to complete a reading comprehension worksheet independently at his desk in the pull-out special education classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Here is your reading comprehension worksheet. Please complete these questions on your own at your desk while I check on the other group.

STUDENT: (Pushes the worksheet away) No, I'm not doing this.

TUTOR: Just try your best and keep working on the questions.

STUDENT: (Starts making loud siren noises and banging his hands on the desk) Ahhhh! Woooo!

TUTOR: Please be quiet and look at your paper.

STUDENT: (Grabs his pencil and throws it at the student sitting next to him, yelling loudly) I said I'm not doing it! Look at me!

options.A: Set a timer to buzz on a fixed 1-minute interval schedule and provide specific performance feedback based on the student's behavior.
options.B: Prompt the student to call on a neighbor, ask a friend, or poll the classroom for help with the reading comprehension worksheet.
options.C: Agree with the student that they are having a rough time with the reading comprehension worksheet during this independent work session.
options.D: Ask a follow-up question that links the student's physical sensation to a potential emotional state regarding the reading comprehension worksheet.
